title: Gradient-span squared-distance lower bound for the path witness
source_anchor: Chewi arXiv:2605.07006v1 §4.2, Exercise 4.1 (printed/PDF p. 28); Definition 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 (p. 26), path quadratic and prefix induction (p. 27), affine minimizer (pp. 27–28); Definition 1.12, Eq. (1.7) (p. 11)
target_statement: Let D and N be natural numbers with 1 ≤ N and 2N+1 ≤ D, let β>0, and prescribe x₀∈ℝᴰ. For v=y−x₀ use the translated path quadratic below and let x★ have centered coordinates 1−k/(D+1), k=1,…,D. The witness is convex, C¹ and satisfies the β quadratic upper model; x★ minimizes it. Every sequence with initial value x₀ and each centered next iterate in the real span of the preceding actual gradients retains at least 1/8 of its initial squared distance to x★ at step N.
